title: Alone with God (Likutey Moharan II:25)
hookLine: an hour a day alone with God, in your own words
tomorrow: seven beggars turn up at a wedding. why are they the gift?

lines: TALKING OUT LOUD ON A LONG DRIVE.
AN HOUR A DAY, IN YOUR OWN WORDS.
WHICH ONE IS THE REAL THING?
cards: Some people talk out loud on long drives, the whole argument, both sides, nobody listening. Rebbe Nachman asked for something close to that, aimed higher.
In Likutey Moharan, part two, teaching twenty-five, he says: set aside an hour or more each day, alone, somewhere private, and speak to God in your own words. Not the prayer book's Hebrew.
The language you actually talk in. So yes, really. But Jewish prayer already has set words, handed down and said day after day.
Which one is the real thing?

teach.b: First, Rebbe Nachman's case. He calls it hitbodedut, making yourself alone. Pour out what's on your heart, the way you'd talk to a true friend: what hurts, what you want, where you keep slipping.

teach.h: EVEN ONE WORD, AGAIN AND AGAIN.
teach.b: If all you can manage is one word, he says, say that one word again and again; even that is good. Set words can roll out of the mouth while the heart is somewhere else. Your own words can't.
Now the other side, and it's old and strong. The Mishnah already worries about prayer that turns into a fixed chore, so the worry isn't new.
But the sages also set down fixed words, and the best case for them goes like this.

teach.h: SET WORDS HOLD YOU WHEN YOU HAVE NONE.
teach.b: They hold you on the days you have no words at all. They're said together: the requests of the Amidah, the standing prayer, say heal us, forgive us, never just me.
And they take you where you'd never go alone, to praise, when you only came to ask. The prayer book is bigger than your mood. Notice what Rebbe Nachman didn't do.
He didn't throw out the prayer book; Breslov Hasidim pray the set services too.
Hitbodedut is added on top, an hour that's yours.
So the two views aren't really fighting over which prayer counts. They're weighing a balance: the words handed down to everyone, and the words only you can say.

how: Breslov Hasidim practice hitbodedut, speaking to God alone in their own words, often outdoors or in a quiet room, alongside the set daily prayers of the siddur.

o: saying the set prayers at home instead of in synagogue
time alone each day to talk with God in your own words
a long silent retreat away from family and friends

games.q: two ways to pray — tap the pairs.
p: said again and again is still good
worries about prayer as a fixed chore
heal us, forgive us, not just me

s: hitbodedut is meant to be said in Hebrew
Rebbe Nachman says to use the language you actually speak.
the worry about prayer becoming a fixed chore is already in the Mishnah
Berakhot 4:4: prayer made fixed is not a plea from the heart.
Rebbe Nachman told his followers to stop praying from the prayer book
hitbodedut is added on top of the set prayers, not instead of them.

games.q: a friend says: 'set prayers are just reciting. only your own words are real prayer.' you want to give the prayer book its best case. what do you say?
o: it holds you on days you have no words, and it prays 'us', not just 'me'.
it's older than anyone's own words, so it must be what God prefers.
it's shorter and quicker than working out what to say on your own.
games.why: the set words hold you when you have none and are said together. Rebbe Nachman didn't drop them; he added an hour of your own on top.

practice: Find the most private spot you can reach right now: a closed door, a parked car, a corner. For the sit, talk quietly, out loud, in your own everyday words; if you pray, to God, and if you don't, to the empty room.
Say what's actually on your mind, and if nothing comes, say one word and let it be enough.

wordCard.voice: Alone with God: Rebbe Nachman's hitbodedut. Time set apart each day to speak to God in your own words, in your own language.

orig.note: Hebrew: making oneself alone; Rebbe Nachman's time each day for talking with God in your own words.

carryVoice: Pocket this: alone with god, an hour that's yours beside the words handed down to everyone. Talk soon.

sources.ref: Likutey Moharan II:25 (hitbodedut: set aside an hour or more daily, alone, to speak to God in one's own language; even a single word repeated is good)
Mishnah Berakhot 4:4 (Rabbi Eliezer: one who makes his prayer keva, fixed, his prayer is not supplication)
